exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Password Guessing
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak authentication mechanisms are directly susceptible to password guessing attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak authentication may allow attackers to bypass proper credential checks using alternate material.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak authentication often involves missing or bypassable MFA, which attackers can exploit or modify.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Reduce Key Space
exploitedBy.relevance: Deprecated cipher suites often use reduced key spaces, making encryption easier to break.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Weaken Encryption
exploitedBy.relevance: Enabling deprecated cipher suites directly weakens encryption protecting communications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted split tunneling allows traffic to bypass network security boundaries, enabling boundary bridging.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol Tunneling
exploitedBy.relevance: Split tunneling can be exploited to tunnel traffic outside of monitored VPN channels.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Conditional Access Policies
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or broad access policies fail to enforce conditional access restrictions, enabling unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Broad network access exposes more remote services to potential exploitation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers can forge or use self-signed certificates similar to those accepted by misconfigured servers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Self-signed or expired certificates can be reconnaissance targets to identify certificate mismanagement.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Environments accepting self-signed certificates are susceptible to certificate forgery attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
exploitedBy.relevance: Unpatched VPN services expose known vulnerabilities in public-facing applications to exploitation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: External Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Long-lived sessions on external remote services increase the window of opportunity for session hijacking.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive session lifetimes increase exposure of session tokens that can be captured via network sniffing.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Externally exposed management interfaces represent an accessible remote service attack surface.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Private Keys
exploitedBy.relevance: Default or shared pre-shared keys are equivalent to compromised private keys that attackers can exploit.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Symmetric Cryptography
exploitedBy.relevance: Pre-shared keys underpin symmetric cryptography; default or shared keys compromise the encryption.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Brute Force
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient logging prevents detection of brute force authentication attacks against the VPN.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Log Enumeration
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers may exploit insufficient logging to avoid detection while enumerating or attacking authentication.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credential Stuffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Without adequate logging, credential stuffing attacks against authentication endpoints go undetected.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Remote Access Tools
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of posture checks allows devices with unauthorized remote access tools to connect to the VPN.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Bypass User Account Control
exploitedBy.relevance: Using privileged accounts for VPN service identity enables privilege escalation if the service is compromised.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Service Execution
exploitedBy.relevance: A VPN service running as a privileged account can be abused for privileged service execution by attackers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Hardcoded secrets in configuration files are directly exposed as credentials stored in files.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Hardcoded secrets represent unsecured credentials accessible to anyone with file system access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Password Spraying
exploitedBy.relevance: No account lockout allows password spraying attacks across multiple accounts without triggering security controls.
